title: Co-culture of Living Microbiome with Microengineered Human Intestinal Villi in a Gut-on-a-Chip Microfluidic Device
protocol: Prepare uncured, degassed PDMS by mixing the PDMS prepolymer and the curing agent (15:1 w/w).
Place the prepared PDMS in a vacuum desiccator for 30 min.
Pour 30 g of uncured, degassed PDMS onto a silicon mold with SU-8 based micropatterns for the upper microchannel.
Pour 3 g of uncured, degassed PDMS onto a silicon mold with SU-8 based micropatterns for the lower microchannel.
Cure both layers at 60 °C in a dry oven for at least 4 hr.
Demold the upper and lower PDMS layers from each silicon mold by cutting around the edge using a surgical scalpel.
Punch 6 holes (two inlets, two outlets, and two vacuum chambers) on each layer using a biopsy puncher (2.0 mm in hole diameter).
Prepare the porous membrane by pouring 10 g of uncured and degassed PDMS on a silanized silicon wafer containing post arrays with circular pillars.
Overlay the poured PDMS with a flat, silanized PDMS support layer (15:1, w/w; 1 cm thick).
Place a 3 kg weight presser on the setup.
Cure the polymer at 60 °C for 12 hr or longer.
Demold the setup of a porous PDMS membrane adhered to the PDMS support slab from the silicon wafer by carefully lifting up the corner of the slab from the wafer.
Peel off until the porous PDMS membrane is completely detached from the wafer.
Expose the channel side of an upper layer (PDMS, 15:1, w/w) and the porous membrane side to the plasma generated by a handheld corona treater for 1 min and 3 sec, respectively.
Place the plasma-treated surfaces of the porous PDMS membrane and upper microchannel layer in a conformal contact without any air bubbles.
Incubate the whole setup at 80 °C O/N for irreversible bonding of the two PDMS layers.
Peel off the PDMS support layer from the assembly of an upper layer with a porous membrane by carefully lifting up the corner of the support layer.
Peel off until the support layer is completely detached from the upper layer with the membrane.
Tear off the portions of this membrane located over the vacuum chambers using a fine-tip tweezers to make hollow vacuum chambers.
Expose the side with the membrane attached on the top piece and the side with the channels engraved on the lower piece to plasma for 1 min.
Align the upper microchannel layer with a porous membrane and the lower layer with a conformal contact by placing each piece in parallel without any air bubbles under a stereoscope.
Cure the whole setup in a dry oven at 80 °C overnight to produce a complete scale gut-on-a-chip microfluidic device.
Connect tubing to the inlet and outlet of each port linked to the upper or lower microchannels via a 90° bent stainless steel blunt-end needle.
Connect the tubing to the holes linked to the vacuum chambers using a 90° bent stainless steel blunt-end needle.
Sterilize the microchannels and tubing by flowing 70% (v/v) ethanol using a 1 ml sterilized disposable syringe.
Dry out the microchannels and tubing in a 60 °C dry oven overnight.
Sterilize the device with 70% (v/v) ethanol using a 1 ml sterilized disposable syringe.
Dry the device in a 60 °C dry oven overnight prior to surface activation.
Expose the complete setup of a gut-on-a-chip microsystem to UV light and ozone simultaneously for 40 min.
Cool down the device at room temperature for 15 min under UV light in a biosafety cabinet.
Mix 100 µl of ECM coating solution containing 50 µg/ml type I collagen and 300 µg/ml extracellular matrix mixture in serum-free DMEM.
Introduce the mixed ECM coating solution into both upper and lower microchannels using a disposable, sterile 1 ml syringe.
Incubate the setup in a 37 °C humidified 5% CO2 incubator for 1 hr.
Degas 50 ml of pre-warmed (37 °C) complete culture medium consisting of DMEM with 20% v/v FBS, 100 units/ml penicillin, and 100 µg/ml streptomycin using a 50 ml filtration system (0.45 µm pore size).
Pass the pre-warmed medium through the filtration system.
Tap gently on the filtered medium for 1 min to remove any bubbles or dissolved gas in the medium.
Place an aliquot of degassed complete medium in a 3 ml disposable syringe and incubate at 37 °C in a humidified 5% CO2 incubator for 1 hr.
Connect two 3 ml disposable syringes containing degassed, pre-warmed complete culture medium to the upper and lower microchannels.

Flow degassed complete cell culture medium into the upper microchannel using a syringe pump at a volumetric flow rate of 30 µl/hr (equivalent to shear stress at 0.02 dyne/cm²) in a 37 °C humidified 5% CO2 incubator overnight.
Use Caco-2BBE cells with passage number between 50 and 65 for the experiment.
Grow Caco-2 cells in a T75 flask containing complete culture medium in a 37 °C humidified 5% CO2 incubator for 4-5 days to obtain fully confluent cells.
Add 10 ml of Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺-free PBS to fully confluent Caco-2 cells, wash the cells, then aspirate out PBS.
Repeat the washing step twice.
Add 1 ml of 0.05% trypsin/EDTA solution and incubate in a 37 °C humidified 5% CO2 incubator for 5 min.
Resuspend the dissociated cells with 10 ml pre-warmed complete cell culture medium by pipetting up and down three to five times.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 500 x g for 5 min, then remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml pre-warmed complete medium to adjust cell density to ~1.5 x 10⁵ cells/cm² in the device.
Estimate the cell density using a hemocytometer.

Infuse 100 μl of the resuspended Caco-2 cells into the upper microchannel (lumen side) by placing a 1 ml disposable syringe attached to a 25 G5/8 needle on the outlet of tubing connected to the upper microchannel.
Clamp all inlets and outlets of tubing connected to the upper and lower microchannels using binder clips.
Incubate the whole setup in a 37 °C, humidified 5% CO2 incubator for 1 hr to allow dissociated Caco-2 cells to adhere to the surface of the porous membrane.
Remove the clamps and resume flow of culture medium only to the upper microchannel at 30 µl/hr using a syringe pump.
Confirm cell-cell junctions in a monolayer using phase contrast or DIC microscopy.
Perfuse culture medium into both upper (lumen) and lower (capillary) microchannels at 30 µl/hr when cells form a monolayer.
Turn on the vacuum pump equipped with tension equipment.
Connect vacuum chambers to the vacuum controller via tubing with a stainless steel connector.
Set stretching motion of 10% mean cell strain at a frequency of 0.15 Hz in cyclic sine function mode on the vacuum controlling software.
Start the mechanical deformation process.
Maintain constant flow of culture medium (30 µl/hr) in both upper and lower microchannels under mechanical deformations for ~100 hr.
Grow microengineered Caco-2 villi by repeating steps from 2.1 to 2.2.
Flow pre-warmed co-culture medium at 30 µl/hr into the upper and lower microchannels.
Introduce 100 µl of dissociated HMVECs into the lower microchannel.
Place a cured rectangular PDMS piece on top of the gut-on-a-chip device.
Flip the whole device setup upside down.
Incubate the setup in a 37 °C, humidified 5% CO2 incubator for 1 hr.
Take out the whole setup from the CO2 incubator.
Flip the setup over again.
Flow pre-warmed co-culture medium at 30 µl/hr into both upper and lower microchannels with mechanical stretching motions (10%, 0.15 Hz).
Perform pre-culture of bacterial cells to co-culture commensal gut microbiome on the microengineered intestinal villi.
Resuspend the freeze-dried probiotic bacterial mixture in 10 ml of a 1:1 (v/v) mixture of autoclaved Lactobacilli MRS Broth and Reinforced Clostridial Medium.
Adjust the final cell density to approximately 0.2 optical density units at 600 nm by adding additional medium as needed.
Aliquot 3 ml of the microbial cell suspension into a 10 ml disposable sterile tube.
Place tubes containing resuspended microbial cells in an anaerobic container.
Add two packs of anaerobic gas generating sachets to the container.
Close the container lid tightly and incubate without shaking at 37 °C in a humidified 5% CO2 incubator overnight.
Prepare 3 ml disposable syringes containing degassed antibiotic-free cell culture medium (DMEM with 20% FBS).
Remove syringes connected to tubing linked to the upper and lower microchannels of the gut-on-a-chip device.
Connect syringes prepared in step 3.2.1 to the device in a biosafety cabinet.
Flow this antibiotic-free culture medium through the gut-on-a-chip device for 12 hours prior to seeding of microbiome.
Spin down pre-cultured probiotic bacterial mixture cells at 10,000 x g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate out the supernatant using vacuum.
Resuspend in antibiotic-free DMEM medium to achieve a final cell density of approximately 1.0 x 10^7 CFU/ml.
Infuse the cell suspension into the lumen side of the microchannel containing "germ-free" intestinal villi using a 1 ml disposable syringe attached to a 25 G5/8 needle.
Allow microbial cells to adhere to the apical surface of the intestinal villi for approximately 1.5 hours without flow by clamping tubing ends.
Perfuse pre-warmed antibiotic-free culture medium into both upper and lower microchannels at 40 µl/hr with cyclic rhythmical deformations (10%, 0.15 Hz).
Pre-cultivate GFP E. coli cells in autoclaved LB medium at 37 °C under shaking condition (200 rpm) for 12 hours.
Repeat steps from infusing the cell suspension to perfusion for co-culture of GFP E. coli cells with microengineered villi.
Take out a gut-on-a-chip microsystem setup from the CO2 incubator.
Place the device setup on the stage of a microscope.
Record microbial and epithelial morphology using DIC, epifluorescence, or laser scanning confocal microscopy.
Flow PBS for washing the cells at 100 µl/hr for 10 min.
Fix villi with 4% (w/v) paraformaldehyde for 15 min.
Flow PBS for washing the cells at 100 µl/hr for 10 min.
Permeabilize the villi with 0.3% (v/v) Triton X-100 diluted in PBS containing 2% (w/v) bovine serum albumin (BSA) for 10 min.
Flow PBS for washing the cells at 100 µl/hr for 10 min.
Block cells with 2% (w/v) BSA solution in PBS for 1 hr.
Flow PBS for washing the cells at 100 µl/hr for 10 min.
Add 300 nM of 4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole dihydrochloride (DAPI) solution diluted in PBS for nuclear staining under light protection.
Add 25 units/ml of fluorescent phalloidin (Phalloidin-CF647 conjugate) dissolved in PBS for F-actin staining under light protection.
Record images of the fluorescently stained cells using a laser scanning confocal microscope.
